factProposals.value: A signed-in staff console at /console: a work order list with status, workflow step, assignee and location, and a detail screen with the full history and GIS record on one screen.
Work orders now record an assignee: an active person allowed to work on work orders, or unassigned; every assignment is audited and versioned.

Staff sign in to the console with their personal key once; the browser keeps only a session token for that tab, the server stores only its hash, and the session ends after 30 minutes idle, 8 hours, sign-out or deactivation.
When GIS does not answer while a work order is opened, the console shows the copy of the GIS record saved when the work order was created, marked as such, and the rest of the screen works.

decisions.statement: Change data from the console only through the existing work order API, using the signed-in person's session.
decisions.rationale: Every console action then lands in the same audit trail, with the same version check, as any API call.
decisions.evidence: server/console/app.js; tests/consoleSessions.test.js (audited exactly like the API)

decisions.statement: Add an assignee to work orders.
decisions.rationale: The console must show who each work order is assigned to, and the system did not record it.

decisions.statement: Check the 1440x900 layout automatically in a headless browser, requiring each screen's own content to appear.
decisions.rationale: The screens are captured for the proposal exhibit; a check by eye can miss overflow, and a fallback page must not pass.

limitations.statement: The console's keep-the-edit-and-retry behaviour after a session expires has been reviewed but is not exercised by an automated test.
The AI intake, map, administration and integrations screens are placeholders until their own stories are built.
The 1440x900 check needs Edge (or another Chromium browser via EDGE_PATH); without it that test is skipped.
